features.evidence: 3 years ... 7 years ... 2, 4, or 6 production services
features.name: Production software depth
features.description: Captures how much relevant shipped-software experience the letter conveys through years, launched services, and signs of ownership.

levels.descriptor: Relevant production experience is unclear, below threshold, or unsupported by concrete scope.
Shows baseline fit, typically a few years of experience or a small number of launched services.
Shows solid mid-level depth, such as several years of work plus multiple production services or clear ownership.
Shows extensive depth, such as long tenure, many launches, and sustained responsibility across services.

features.evidence: Bachelor's ... Master's ... Doctoral degree
features.name: Academic credential level
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education the letter cites in a relevant field.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.evidence: Python is production-grade, not just scripting
features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how concretely and convincingly the letter shows Python as a production language for services, automation, or tooling.

levels.descriptor: No Python evidence, or Python is only named without context.
Python is mentioned for basic scripting or generic use.
Shows substantial production Python use in services, automation, or internal tooling.
Shows deep production Python use with quality signals such as typed, tested, extensible, or central security tooling.

features.evidence: Python agents plan and act while Go services provide the guardrails
features.name: Agentic architecture ownership
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows hands-on design of agentic systems, especially the split between Python agents and Go infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic system experience is shown.
Mentions agents or agentic tooling only at a high level.
Describes building agent-based tooling with a clear role split between components.
Shows end-to-end agentic design with bounded actions, permissions, auditing, or supervision.

features.evidence: evaluation scaffolding required to deploy them responsibly
features.name: AI deployment maturity
features.description: Captures the level of real production AI experience, especially whether the letter addresses reliability, evaluation, or hardening rather than novelty alone.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without meaningful deployment detail.
Shows shipped AI features or model-backed workflows in production.
Shows production AI work plus explicit evaluation, reliability, or hardening practices.

features.evidence: classification and routing layer
features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures whether the letter gives direct evidence of automating intake, classification, deduplication, or routing of vulnerability reports.

levels.descriptor: No triage automation evidence appears.
Expresses interest in automating security response but gives no owned example.
Clearly describes building vulnerability intake or triage automation.
Describes triage automation with concrete workflow elements such as classification, deduplication, routing, or stated operational impact.

features.evidence: threat models and follow-through
features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures how directly the letter shows hands-on security review work such as threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, code review, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.evidence: replaced ad-hoc traversals with proper graph algorithms
features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through specific engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic evidence is given.
Makes a generic claim about data structures or algorithms.
Gives a specific example of choosing a better structure or redesigning logic algorithmically.
Gives a strong example showing substantial performance, scalability, or tractability improvement from algorithmic skill.

features.evidence: improvements there are inherited by every team downstream
features.name: Foundational leverage motivation
features.description: Captures how strongly the letter is motivated by central infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams or systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows no clear attraction to platform-scale leverage.
Mentions scale or central impact only in passing.
Clearly values foundational or core infrastructure work.
Makes compounded downstream impact a central and convincing reason for applying.

features.evidence: do the secure thing by default
features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security tooling as helping developers through defaults and reduced friction rather than policing or process.

levels.descriptor: No clear service orientation toward other engineers is shown.
Uses general collaboration or helpfulness language.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or proactively assisting developers.
Makes secure defaults, time savings, and low-friction tooling core to the case for fit.

features.evidence: software that guards other software must be built to a higher standard
features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a crisp point of view about what security engineering is for and how it should be practiced.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinct point of view beyond wanting the job.
Uses generic statements about liking security or impact.
States a clear principle or worldview about security engineering.
Uses a memorable principle that frames the letter and signals mature judgment.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned
features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how much the letter backs claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, or outcomes rather than broad assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.evidence: CompTIA Security+ ... OSCP
features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the rigor of formal security credentials cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or equivalent fundamentals.
Mentions a demanding practical credential such as OSCP or equivalent.

features.evidence: top placements in several large open competitions
features.name: Offensive practice intensity
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows ongoing adversarial practice through capture-the-flag participation and how serious that practice is.

levels.descriptor: No ongoing offensive practice is shown.
Mentions CTF participation or practice without strong results.
Shows serious practice with top or near-top competitive results.

features.evidence: maintainer of an open-source tooling project used well beyond my own team
features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows responsibility for a public project with external users or contributors.

levels.descriptor: No public project stewardship is shown.
Mentions public code or contributions without ownership responsibilities.
Maintains a public project with users or contributors and handles reviews, releases, or roadmap.

features.evidence: write and submit the patches upstream
features.name: Upstream repair habit
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows a habit of fixing defects in dependencies or tools at the source instead of only working around them locally.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of upstream fixing appears.
Mentions occasional or general upstream contributions.
Shows a clear recurring habit of writing and shepherding patches to source projects.

features.evidence: replicated log store with failover from first principles
features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures how much the letter uses side projects to demonstrate sustained engineering curiosity and technical range.

levels.descriptor: No side project evidence is given.
Mentions a small utility, hobby app, or modest build mainly as a curiosity signal.
Mentions a substantial self-driven system with meaningful complexity such as distributed coordination, storage, failover, or recovery.

features.evidence: engnieer ... spnt ... misssion
features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures how free the letter is from distracting typos, misspellings, and copy errors.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors distract from credibility and care.
A few noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
The copy is clean or nearly clean.

features.evidence: I started my career on the unglamorous side of software
features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents the applicant through a memorable, coherent narrative rather than a template-like inventory of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Reads like a formulaic list of qualifications.
Shows some personality or framing but remains mostly conventional.
Presents a memorable personal arc or framing that helps the letter stand out.

features.evidence: absorb the craft from people who practice it daily
features.name: Learning posture
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents the candidate as coachable and motivated to deepen security expertise through collaboration with specialists.

levels.descriptor: Shows no sign of wanting to grow through security collaboration.
Shows indirect openness to learning or collaboration.
Explicitly emphasizes learning from security engineers or deepening security craft on the job.
